newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Gazprom mandates ABN, Goldman for $2-3 bn programme.
newsitem.headline: Gazprom mandates ABN, Goldman for $2-3 bn programme.

text.p: Russian gas monopoly RAO Gazprom has mandated Dutch bank ABN-Amro and U.S. investment bank Goldman Sachs to arrange a $2-3 billion financing programme, ABN-Amro's country manager for Russia said on Monday.

They said they expected to issue a Eurobond with a minimum size of $1 billion, and convertible bonds with a volume of $500 million to $1 billion, for Gazprom, both within six months, Frank Kuijlaars said. Within one month Gazprom will receive a bridging loan of $500 million to $1 billion, he told Reuters.
"The programme will settle somewhere between $2 billion and $3 billion," Kuijlaars told bankers.

ABN-Amro managing board member Jan Maarten de Jong said the package had been agreed on Friday. "The bank only quite recently, only last Friday, more or less finalised a mandate for a major financial transaction with Gazprom, along with Goldman Sachs," he said.
He said the package included a bridge finance element because Gazprom needed the money before it would be able to bring its bonds to market.

Gazprom has already issued American Depositary Shares which allow foreign trading of its equity. Share analysts do not expect Gazprom to issue more ADSs soon because of controversy surrounding restrictions on foreign ownership of Gazprom domestic stock, which trades at about one third of the price of the ADS. Details of the planned convertible bond issue were not immediately available.
